title: U.S. House · California's 26th District
area: Most of Ventura County and a small portion of Los Angeles County, including Thousand Oaks, Oxnard, Camarillo, Santa Paula, Moorpark, Westlake Village, and part of Simi Valley. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.

This is an open seat: incumbent Democrat Julia Brownley did not seek re-election to this district in 2026. Democrat Jacqui Irwin, currently a member of the California State Assembly, won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 41.3% of the vote; Republican Samuel Gallucci advanced with 20.9%.

candidates.name: Jacqui Irwin
candidates.currentRole: Member, California State Assembly, District 42 (since 2022; term ends December 2026)
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 primary with 41.3% of the vote

summary.text: Jacqui Irwin is the Democratic nominee for California's 26th Congressional District, an open seat. A systems engineer by training, she served on the Thousand Oaks City Council, including two terms as mayor, before her 2014 election to the California State Assembly, where she currently represents the 42nd District. She launched her congressional campaign in January 2026 after Rep. Julia Brownley announced her retirement.

background.text: Graduated from Taft High School in Woodland Hills, California, and earned a bachelor of science in systems engineering from UC San Diego in 1985.
Worked as an engineer at Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Lab and at Teledyne Systems.
Appointed to the Thousand Oaks Planning Commission in 2003, elected to the Thousand Oaks City Council in 2004, and later served two terms as mayor of Thousand Oaks.
Elected to the California State Assembly in 2014 from the 44th District, defeating Republican Rob McCoy 52.3% to 47.7%; re-elected in 2016, 2018, and 2020, and in 2022 from the redrawn 42nd District.
In the 2025-2026 Assembly session, chairs the Climate Change Policies Committee.

Launched her campaign for the 26th Congressional District on January 8, 2026, after Rep. Julia Brownley announced she would not seek re-election, and advanced from the June 2 primary with 41.3% of the vote.
According to Wikipedia, she married Jon Irwin in 1986 and has three children; Ballotpedia lists her residence as Thousand Oaks.

record.text: In the 2025-2026 California State Assembly session, serves as chair of the Climate Change Policies Committee and as a member of the Agriculture, Business and Professions, Privacy and Consumer Protection, Rules, Utilities and Energy, and Fairs, Allocation, and Classification committees.

candidates.name: Samuel Gallucci
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary with 20.9% of the vote

summary.text: Samuel (Sam) Gallucci is the Republican nominee for California's 26th Congressional District. He is a pastor in Oxnard and a business executive, and he previously ran in the 2021 California gubernatorial recall election. His ballot designation is Business Executive/Pastor.

background.text: Ran as a Republican candidate on the 2021 California gubernatorial recall replacement ballot, receiving 18,134 votes, according to JoinCalifornia.
He and his wife, Toni, are listed as lead pastors of Embrace Church in Oxnard on the church's website.
JoinCalifornia lists him as married to Toni with three sons.

researchNotes: Neither Jacqui Irwin nor Samuel Gallucci has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Irwin's sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia did not render usable content within this session, so record is limited to her Assembly committee roles; her campaign website was not identifiable via Ballotpedia's infobox within the time budget. Re-checked https://ballotpedia.org/Samuel_Gallucci (September 2026): no biography section and no Candidate Connection survey for 2026 or his 2021 recall run; his campaign website (https://samgallucci.com/) again loaded with no usable text content (JavaScript-rendered). His entry stays minimal; no other public statements of his positions were found. Biography gaps: Gallucci's campaign site renders no text without JavaScript, so his career and education come from secondary profiles (The Ballot Brief and Prediction Edge, both aggregators) and are attributed; birthplace, birth year, and years of employment were not found.
